item.text: {"claim_count":66,"content_failure_reasons":["The claim that the authorities emphasized fiscal discipline as one of the factors helping Mexico through the pandemic and recent tightening period is not supported by the cited authorities’ views on p. 23, ¶34. That passage discusses the flexible exchange rate, remittances, resurgent FDI, and reduced foreign participation in local-currency sovereign bonds; fiscal discipline appears elsewhere as staff discussion."],"content_usable":true,"material_omission":true,"material_omission_explanation":"The map omits staff’s assessment in p. 21, ¶30 that public debt remained sustainable and was expected to stay broadly unchanged over the next decade, subject to weaker-growth and adjustment-slippage risks. It also omits the authorities’ statement in pp. 21–22, ¶31 that support during a shock could be financed by reallocating spending away from public investment. These are material qualifications for fiscal resilience and public-investment evidence, but the remaining map is sufficiently extensive and balanced for chapter use, so the omissions do not make it unusable.","schema_version":"reader_content_audit_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","supported_claim_count":65,"unsupported_claim_count":1,"usable_locator_count":65}
